title: Reconcile quota charges for prefetch tokens and coalesced batch accounting
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Several customers and internal billing reports show discrepancies when prefix/KV cache hits and request coalescing (server-side batch aggregation) are present. Billing currently double-counts some tokens in coalesced flows and charges for prefetch-prefilled tokens inconsistently across Hosted vs Dedicated deployments. This ticket defines deterministic rules for how cached tokens and coalesced batches affect quota depletion, per-request metering, and rate-limiter accounting, together with an implementation plan and tests.

Background: We observed three related issues: (1) prefix cache hits were being included in invoiced 'input tokens' in some code paths, (2) KV-cache prefetch that populates cache before a later request isn't accounted uniformly and sometimes gets billed to the wrong customer project, and (3) when the runtime coalesces multiple independent requests into a single forward pass (coalescing), token charges are being assigned at the batch level and then re-applied per-request in the billing pipeline resulting in overcharging. Existing tickets (ENG-8632, ENG-9271) touched metering normalization; this work finalizes allocation rules and implements safe migration.

Goals:
- Define unambiguous billing rules for prefix cache hits and KV cache prefetch: when they are free, when they are billable, and which customer/route is charged.
- Specify token allocation algorithm for coalesced batches so each logical request is charged fairly and deterministically.
- Ensure rate limits and quota checks remain protective (prevent abuse) while aligning invoicing with observed compute.
- Add unit/integration tests, dashboards, and a migration for historical reprocessing only if necessary.

Scope (non-goals): This ticket does not change pricing tiers or per-token prices. It does not modify per-route SLA throttling behavior except to fix incorrect quota decrements.

Proposed rules (decision draft):
1) Prefix cache (server-side prefix/KV cache used to short-circuit decoding): prefix cache hits for prompt tokens that were never executed on GPU should not incur compute token charges. They can still count against 'request count' rate limits.
2) KV-cache prefetch: if a prefetch is triggered by an authenticated customer request and is for that customer's namespace, do not bill the prefetch separately when a subsequent request reuses the cached KV entries. If a cache fill originates from background work not attributable to a customer (e.g., model warm-up), bill to platform costs (do not attribute to customer).
3) Coalesced batch token allocation: when N logical requests are coalesced into one forward: compute the total tokens produced by the aggregated forward. Allocate compute tokens to each logical request proportional to its contribution to sequence length (prompt+expected generation length) at coalesce time. For deterministic auditing, store the allocation map in the trace for each request.
4) Edge cases: for partial KV cache hits (some layers hit, some miss) charge only for the miss portions. For streaming partial responses where later tokens are served from cache, adjust allocation during the stream and emit a corrective billing delta recorded in the request trace.

Acceptance criteria:
- Billing service applies new allocation rules to live traffic for a shadow period and reports a <0.5% customer-facing delta except for workloads dominated by prefetch (expected behavior).
- Unit tests cover: prefix-cache-only hit (0 compute tokens billed), full-KV-prefetch flow (no double-charge), 3-way coalesced batch allocation proportionality, and streaming corrective deltas.
- Integration test with rate limiter: quota checks still prevent request admission even when cache would later make the request free; quotas show pre/post-change parity for non-cache-heavy workloads.
- Audit log/tracing: every billed invoice line references the request trace id and allocation map for reproducing ledger decisions.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (shadow): implement allocation logic in billing core and runtime hooks to emit allocation events. Route billing changes behind a feature flag and run in shadow mode for 2 weeks. (Owner: Liam)
- Phase 2 (QA + compliance review): run integration tests, compliance audit (Finance + Security). Add acceptance criteria dashboards. (Owner: Maya)
- Phase 3 (gradual rollout): enable flag for 10% of production, monitor per-customer deltas, then 50%, then 100%. Publish change notes and update developer docs.

Testing & validation:
- Add unit tests for allocation math and prefix/KV decision trees.
- Create integration scenario harness that simulates prefetch flows, cross-customer cache contamination attempts, and coalesced low-latency burst traffic.
- Migration: if historical ledgers must be reprocessed for a small set of accounts (high discrepancy), perform targeted reprocessing post-approval; otherwise record adjustment credits.

Observability:
- New Grafana panels (dashboard link below) to show billed_tokens_vs_compute_tokens, coalesced_batch_allocation_distrib, prefix_cache_hit_billing_rate.
- Emit a new telemetry tag "billing.allocation_map" that holds a compact allocation signature for each coalesced request (stored in traces for 90 days).

Docs & communications:
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILL/Coalesce+and+Cache+Billing+Spec
- Developer blog + changelog entry to explain change and examples for customers.
- Finance runbook for refund/credit decisions if customers see unexpected deltas.

Migration & rollback:
- Feature-gated rollout with immediate rollback possible by disabling gating.
- Keep shadow logs for 90 days to support post-incident accounting audits.

Notes on rate limits and quotas interaction:
- Rate limits (requests per minute) remain based on logical request admission before coalescing. This prevents bypass via aggregation.
- Quota (token budget) decrements happen after allocation calculation so that billed tokens reflect computed usage. However, quota enforcement for burst protection must check pre-alloc estimates to avoid letting extremely large aggregated forwards slip through. Implement a conservative pre-check: if aggregate estimated tokens > single-request quota threshold, reject prior to coalescing.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Slightly increased billing pipeline complexity and storage of allocation metadata. Trade-off is improved customer fairness and reduced dispute volume.
- Possible minor increases in latency while calculating allocation map in high-concurrency coalescing. Mitigate with lightweight heuristics and optimized path for common case.

Links and artifacts: 
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILL/Coalesce+and+Cache+Billing+Spec
- GitHub PR (implementation): https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/482
- Integration harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-integration-tests/tree/eng-9412
- Grafana dashboard (internal): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd1234/coalesce-cache-billing
acceptance_criteria: 1) Shadow run reports <0.5% delta for non-cache-heavy customers; 2) Unit + integration tests for 5 named scenarios pass; 3) Allocation map persisted in traces for all coalesced forwards; 4) Finance review sign-off on runbook for customer credits.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout: shadow (2w) -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%. Monitor per-customer delta, error rates, and latency. Communicate in /releases and customer changelog. Revert by toggling feature flag if >2% unexpected deltas or any P0 incidents.
comments: 2025-11-10 Maya Chen: Initial draft of allocation rules pushed to Confluence. Requested feedback from Finance and Runtime team.
2025-11-11 Diego Alvarez (Finance): Flagged concern about attribution of prefetch when background warmups are present; agreed platform-level cost attribution for non-auth prefetches.
2025-11-12 Priya Rao (Runtime): Confirmed we can emit allocation_map in request trace with negligible overhead; will add an in-memory fast-path for common two-request coalesces.
2025-11-13 Liam O'Neill: WIP implementation in billing/core; opened PR #482 for review. Adding unit tests for proportional allocation.

2025-11-14 Code review (Ben Carter): Left comments on edge-case for streaming corrective deltas — prefer additive billing delta records rather than replacing previous lines. Also suggested tighter pre-checks to avoid quota bypass.
